A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 22-page versions of Embodied-Reasoner. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated related work and renumbered appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulator evaluations of Embodied-Reasoner and its training stages in Table 2, plus experiments on 30 real-world tasks in Section 5.3 and Table B1.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulator results in Table 2 and the 30-task real-world evaluation in Section 5.3 and Table A1.

M1.justification: The trajectory-synthesis procedure, Qwen2-VL-7B base model, and three training stages—imitation learning, rejection sampling and reflection tuning—remain unchanged, including anomaly insertion and loss masking.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four AI2-THOR task families and real-world scenarios. Newly cited benchmarks such as ALFRED, GOAT-Bench and OpenEQA are contextual references, with no corresponding evaluations added.

E2.justification: Table 2, Figures 5–6 and the real-world table retain their comparator sets. Table B1 in v1 matches Table A1 in v2; newly cited embodied-agent methods are not added as experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The 9,390 training trajectories, 809 test cases across 12 novel scenes, evaluation metrics and testing procedures are unchanged. Both retain the 50-case manual Kimi-K1.5 evaluation and human-operated real-world protocol.

E4.justification: Training-stage comparisons, task-length and reasoning-token analyses in Figure 5, repetitive exploration analysis in Figure 6, and dataset analyses are retained. The same three case studies move from Appendix F to Appendix E.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is introduced or removed.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative outcomes are unchanged. Table 2 retains 80.96% overall success for Embodied-Reasoner and 71.73% for GPT-o1; real-world Table B1/A1 retains 56.7% and 50.0%, respectively. Appendix plots and case outcomes also match.

T1.justification: Trajectory notation, reflection-training expressions, formal task constraints and metric definitions are retained. There are no added or revised theoretical statements, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims: an embodied reasoning corpus, a three-stage training pipeline, and advantages on complex interactive tasks and real-world search.

C2.justification: Interpretations connecting reasoning to efficient search and reduced repetition remain unchanged. Both retain the simple-search over-exploration limitation and the explanation that additional checking raises Reasoner's repetition relative to Explorer.

D1.justification: Training-data details, task templates, constraint checks, interaction and feedback prompts, and the project-link disclosure are unchanged. Templates and prompts are renumbered from Appendices D–E to C–D without technical additions.

R1.justification: v2 retains the original 66 references and adds 11, including ALFRED, Code as Policies, LLM-Planner, GOAT-Bench and Agent-Pro. These support a limited expansion of discussion about embodied planning, navigation and autonomous reasoning; the central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The largely retained three-part Related Works section moves from Appendix A to main Section 6. Conclusions becomes Section 7 and the remaining appendices are renumbered. Other changes are localized wording and hyphenation edits.

P2.justification: The section move and expanded bibliography reflow pages and appendix floats. Real-world Table B1 becomes A1, dataset Figures C1–C8 become B1–B8, and case figures are relabeled. Their contents and display structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 gives the previously generic discussion of embodied planning and navigation more concrete citation support and makes related work accessible in main Section 6. This modestly improves scholarly context and organization, while the methods, empirical evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
